headline: Philadelphia leads a high-scoring midweek round
dek: Fourteen games across four days produced 46 goals, two draws, and no shortage of momentum shifts deep in the standings race.
body: Philadelphia Union posted the round's biggest margin, beating Orlando City SC 4-2 on Sept. 26. CF Montréal followed with a 3-1 home win over FC Cincinnati the same night. Chicago Fire FC won away at Charlotte FC, 1-0. Seattle Sounders FC swept a home double-header, blanking Real Salt Lake 2-0 on Sept. 24 then beating Minnesota United 3-1 on Sept. 27. Sporting Kansas City won 2-0 at Houston Dynamo. FC Dallas edged LAFC 1-0 and Real Salt Lake recovered to beat New England Revolution 3-0. LA Galaxy won 3-2 over Colorado, Nashville SC beat Toronto 2-0, and San Jose Earthquakes downed Portland Timbers 3-1. Atlanta United and NYCFC, and Vancouver Whitecaps and D.C. United, each finished 3-3. Austin FC and San Diego FC drew 3-3.

headline: Cuypers exits to Monterrey; Izoita signs first-team deal
dek: Three departures and two confirmed arrivals reshape rosters with weeks left in the regular season.
body: Hugo Cuypers has left Chicago Fire FC for CF Monterrey in Liga MX, ending a stint of 990 minutes in 2026. Iván Jaime's loan from FC Porto expired at season's end and CF Montréal declined the purchase option, returning the Spanish midfielder to Porto after 1,050 minutes this season. Chris Cappis departs FC Dallas after logging 1,080 minutes in 2026. On the arrivals side, Portland Timbers have signed academy product Eric Izoita to a first-team MLS contract, accelerating a deal that had been set to begin in 2027. St. Louis CITY SC have acquired goalkeeper Zack Campagnolo on loan from Colorado Rapids for the remainder of 2026.

headline: Musa leads at 18; assist table deadlocked at the top
dek: FC Dallas's striker holds a one-goal edge with the Western Conference still to be settled.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas leads the goals chart with 18, one ahead of Vancouver's Brian White at 17 and Nashville's Sam Surridge at 16. In assists, Albert Rusnák of Seattle Sounders FC and San Diego FC's Anders Dreyer share the lead at 11, with Son Heung-Min of LAFC three back at 10. In the tackle count, Vancouver's Andrés Cubas has put the race out of reach with 100 on the season, with Inter Miami's Yannick Bright next at 77 and D.C. United's Silvan Hefti at 64.

headline: Guilherme and Fernández beat their xG; Almirón trails his by 5.1
dek: The gap between expected goals and actual output tells different stories at either end of the table.
body: Houston Dynamo's Guilherme leads the overperformers, scoring 14 goals against an xG of 6.7, a positive difference of plus-7.3. NYCFC's Nicolás Fernández sits second, with 15 goals on an xG of 8.6, plus-6.4. On the other side, Atlanta United's Miguel Almirón has converted just 4 goals despite an xG of 9.1, a deficit of minus-5.1. Inter Miami's Germán Berterame is minus-4.2, with 7 goals on 11.2 xG. Nashville SC lead the East at 60 points on an 18W-6D-3L record, conceding only 21 goals, the league's best defensive mark. Vancouver Whitecaps top the West with 50 points.

headline: Seattle shuts out RSL; Miami and San Diego split points
dek: The Sounders move to 2-0 at home in their last two while Inter Miami's lead at the top of the goals column stays under pressure.
body: Seattle Sounders FC defeated Real Salt Lake 2-0 on Sept. 24, extending their grip on the Western Conference race with a clean sheet at Lumen Field. RSL, who logged 544 minutes from defender Juan José Arias this season before his departure, offered little going forward. On Sept. 20, Inter Miami CF and San Diego FC played to a 2-2 draw at Chase Stadium. Anders Dreyer, who sits on 10 assists for San Diego, was central to their attack. Miami remain the league's most prolific side with 63 goals scored.

headline: Three MLS midfielders and defenders exit league rosters
dek: A Liga MX transfer, a contract termination, and a loan conclusion clear three names from the MLS record before the playoff run.
body: LA Galaxy transferred midfielder Edwin Cerrillo to Liga MX side Club América for an undisclosed fee, closing out a 1,320-minute 2026 campaign. Sporting Kansas City mutually terminated the contract of Spanish midfielder Manu García, who logged 1,470 minutes this season and had occupied a Designated Player slot; Sporting KC also exercised a buyout of his guaranteed contract. Real Salt Lake defender Juan José Arias, who accumulated 544 minutes this season, has also departed the club's MLS roster.

headline: Musa leads at 18; three players deadlocked on assists at 10
dek: FC Dallas's striker holds a two-goal cushion at the top while the assist table is a three-way tie heading into the final weeks.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas leads all scorers with 18 goals, two clear of Sam Surridge (Nashville SC) and Brian White (Vancouver Whitecaps), who are level on 16. The assists race is knotted at 10 apiece among Son Heung-Min of LAFC, Cristian Espinoza of Nashville SC, and Anders Dreyer of San Diego FC. In the tackles chart, Vancouver's Andrés Cubas stands alone at 100, 23 clear of Yannick Bright of Inter Miami (77) and 39 ahead of D.C. United's Silvan Hefti (61).

headline: Guilherme runs 7.5 goals above xG; Almirón sits 5.1 below
dek: Houston's forward and two underperformers highlight the widest xG gaps in the league this season.
body: Houston Dynamo FC forward Guilherme leads MLS in positive xG differential, scoring 14 goals against an xG of 6.5, a gap of plus-7.5. New York City FC's Nicolás Fernández is second at plus-6.6, with 15 goals on 8.4 xG. At the other end, Atlanta United's Miguel Almirón has converted just 4 goals from 9.1 xG, a deficit of minus-5.1. Inter Miami's Germán Berterame sits at minus-4.2, scoring 7 on an xG of 11.2. Nashville SC lead the East on 57 points (17W-6D-3L), conceding just 21 goals all season. Vancouver Whitecaps top the West with 49 points on 15W-4D-6L.

headline: Philadelphia, Vancouver, Nashville lead road sweep
dek: Sixteen matches across six days handed visitors the edge on the scoreboard and tightened the Western race.
body: Philadelphia Union took four points from their two road appearances, beating Sporting Kansas City 4-3. Nashville SC blanked Chicago Fire 3-0 to stay top of the East on 57 points (17W-6D-3L). Vancouver Whitecaps won 3-0 at Real Salt Lake before Seattle Sounders went to Colorado and drew 3-3. LA Galaxy edged Minnesota United 3-2. Atlanta United won 1-0 in Portland. St. Louis beat Toronto 3-1. In the Hudson River Derby, Red Bull New York won 1-0 at NYCFC. New England beat Orlando City 4-2. Seattle then beat Real Salt Lake again on Sept. 24, 2-0, extending RSL's difficult run. Houston-Cincinnati and Inter Miami-San Diego each ended 2-2.

headline: Three out, three in as rosters reset before playoffs
dek: A pair of overseas transfers and a homegrown promotion headline a busy week of MLS roster activity.
body: Defender Miki Yamane departs LA Galaxy for Urawa Red Diamonds of the J1 League after logging 1,380 minutes this season. Forward Woobens Pacius leaves Nashville SC for FC Rouen 1899 in France's Ligue 3 after 900 minutes in 2026. Winger Zavier Gozo exits Real Salt Lake for Crystal Palace in the Premier League after 1,470 minutes; RSL described it as a club-record transfer. On the inbound side, former Manchester United left back Tyrell Malacia signs with FC Cincinnati on a free transfer through June 2027. Red Bull New York convert homegrown winger Dennis Nelich, 18, to a full MLS contract through the 2027-28 season.

headline: Musa leads at 18; three players locked at 10 assists
dek: The individual stat races are crowded at the top with five weeks of regular season still to play.
body: FC Dallas forward Petar Musa holds the Golden Boot lead with 18 goals. Nashville SC's Sam Surridge and Vancouver's Brian White share second at 16. The assists table is a three-way tie: LAFC's Son Heung-Min, Nashville's Cristian Espinoza, and San Diego FC's Anders Dreyer each have 10. In the tackling chart, Vancouver's Andrés Cubas sits at an imposing 100 tackles, 23 clear of Inter Miami's Yannick Bright (77) and 39 ahead of D.C. United's Silvan Hefti (61).

headline: Guilherme 7.5 goals above xG; Almirón 5.1 below
dek: The league's finishing data reveals stark gaps between expectation and output at both ends of the table.
body: Houston Dynamo's Guilherme leads all overperformers with 14 goals on just 6.5 xG, a positive gap of 7.5. NYCFC's Nicolás Fernández is next at plus-6.6, converting 15 goals from 8.4 xG. At the other end, Atlanta United's Miguel Almirón has scored only 4 goals against 9.1 xG, a deficit of 5.1. Inter Miami's Germán Berterame is second-worst, producing 7 goals from 11.2 xG, sitting 4.2 below expectation.
